senses.def: happening at the end of a process or series of events
ex: Our ultimate aim is to open a school.
The ultimate decision belongs to the manager.

senses.def: the best or most extreme example of something
ex: For many people, this is the ultimate holiday.

senses.def: finally, after everything else has been considered or has happened
ex: Ultimately, it is your decision.
The project ultimately failed.

senses.def: not able to do something
ex: She was unable to attend the meeting.
He is unable to walk without help.

mistake.note: Unable is followed by a to-infinitive, not 'of' + -ing.

senses.def: too bad or wrong to be allowed
ex: Rude behaviour is unacceptable in this school.
The noise level is unacceptable.

senses.def: pure, with nothing added or mixed in
ex: The shop sells unadulterated honey.
It was unadulterated joy.

senses.def: done without official permission
ex: Unauthorized people may not enter this room.
There was an unauthorized use of her credit card.

senses.def: not able to be obtained or used, or not free to see someone
ex: The product is currently unavailable.
The manager is unavailable until Monday.

senses.def: not knowing about something
ex: He was unaware of the danger.
She seemed unaware that everyone was watching.

mistake.wrong: He was unaware about the problem.
mistake.right: He was unaware of the problem.

senses.def: too painful or unpleasant to accept or put up with
ex: The heat was unbearable.
The pain became unbearable.

senses.def: so surprising or extreme that it is difficult to believe
ex: The view from the top was unbelievable.
It's unbelievable that he forgot again.

senses.def: strange and difficult to explain
ex: There was an uncanny silence in the house.
She bears an uncanny resemblance to her grandmother.

senses.def: the brother of your mother or father, or the husband of your aunt
ex: My uncle lives in Canada.
Uncle Ali is coming to dinner.

senses.def: not usual or not often found
ex: It is uncommon to see snow here.
This bird is now very uncommon.

senses.def: in a state like sleep, not able to see, feel or think, usually after an injury
ex: He was knocked unconscious in the fall.
The patient remained unconscious for two days.

senses.def: done without realising that you are doing it
ex: She made an unconscious gesture of surprise.

senses.def: different from what is usual or accepted
ex: She has an unconventional way of teaching.
He led an unconventional life.

senses.def: in or to a lower position than something, often covered by it
ex: The cat is under the table.
She hid the letter under her pillow.

senses.def: less than a number, amount or age
ex: Children under five travel free.
It cost under ten pounds.

senses.def: to think that something is smaller, easier or less important than it really is
ex: Don't underestimate how difficult the exam is.
They underestimated the cost of the repairs.

senses.def: below the surface of the ground
ex: There is an underground car park.
Underground water supplies are running low.

senses.def: below the surface of the ground
ex: The cables are buried underground.

senses.def: to make something or someone gradually weaker or less effective
ex: Constant criticism can undermine confidence.
The scandal undermined public trust in the government.
These results undermine the original theory.

mistake.note: undermine takes a direct object, with no preposition.

senses.def: directly below something, often covered by it
ex: The keys were underneath the newspaper.
She wore a T-shirt underneath her jacket.

senses.def: in a lower position
ex: I lifted the box and found a coin underneath.

senses.def: to know what something means or how it works
ex: I don't understand this word.
Do you understand how to use it?

senses.def: to know why someone feels or behaves in a certain way
ex: I understand why you are angry.

mistake.wrong: I am understanding the lesson now.
mistake.note: Understand is a state verb and is not normally used in continuous tenses.

senses.def: normal and easy to accept in the situation
ex: Her anger is understandable.
It's understandable that you feel nervous.

senses.def: able to be understood
ex: The instructions should be understandable to everyone.

senses.def: showing sympathy and kindness towards other people's feelings
ex: My boss was very understanding about my illness.

senses.def: knowledge of how something works or what it means
ex: She has a good understanding of the subject.

senses.def: an informal agreement between people
ex: We have an understanding that he pays on Fridays.

senses.def: clothes worn next to the skin under other clothes
ex: She packed socks and underwear for the trip.

mistake.right: He bought two pairs of underwear.
mistake.note: Underwear is uncountable, so use 'pairs of' to count it.

senses.def: to open something that is tied, fastened or buttoned
ex: She undid her seat belt.
Can you undo this knot?

senses.def: to remove the effect of something that was done
ex: Press this button to undo your last change.
You cannot undo the damage.

senses.def: used to say that something is certainly true
ex: She is undoubtedly the best player in the team.
This is undoubtedly a serious problem.

senses.def: to take your clothes off, or take someone else's clothes off
ex: The child undressed and got into bed.
She undressed the baby for her bath.

senses.def: not wearing clothes
ex: I was still undressed when he knocked.
Get undressed and put on your pyjamas.

senses.def: without a job although you are able to work
ex: He has been unemployed for six months.
Many young people are unemployed.

senses.def: the situation of not having a job, or the number of people without jobs
ex: Unemployment is high in the region.
The government wants to reduce unemployment.

senses.def: completely clear, with no doubt about the meaning
ex: The minister gave an unequivocal answer.
There is unequivocal evidence of fraud.

senses.def: in a way that is completely clear and leaves no doubt
ex: The president unequivocally rejected the claim.
She stated unequivocally that she would resign.

senses.def: surprising because you did not expect it
ex: We had an unexpected visitor.
The result was completely unexpected.

senses.def: not known or not seen before
ex: The streets were unfamiliar to her.
He felt nervous in unfamiliar surroundings.

senses.def: not knowing much about something
ex: I am unfamiliar with this software.

senses.def: having bad luck, or happening because of bad luck
ex: It was an unfortunate accident.
The unfortunate man lost his job and his home.

senses.def: used to say that you are sorry or disappointed about something
ex: Unfortunately, I can't come to your party.
The shop was closed, unfortunately.

senses.def: the same in all parts or at all times
ex: The room was kept at a uniform temperature.
The houses were of uniform size.

senses.def: special clothes worn by the members of a group, such as a school, army or company
ex: Our school uniform is blue and white.
The police officer was in uniform.

senses.def: so extreme or strange that it is difficult to imagine
ex: The family suffered unimaginable pain.
Ten years ago, this technology was unimaginable.

senses.def: an organisation of workers that protects their rights and interests
ex: The union demanded higher pay for teachers.
He joined the trade union.

senses.def: the act of joining together, or a group of countries or states joined together
ex: The European Union has many members.

senses.def: being the only one of its kind
ex: Every person's fingerprints are unique.
The museum offers a unique chance to see the manuscripts.

mistake.note: Unique already means 'one of a kind', so avoid very before it.

senses.def: doing or saying something at exactly the same time as other people
ex: The students answered in unison.
They moved in perfect unison.

senses.def: a single complete thing, or a part of a larger whole
ex: Each unit of the course lasts two weeks.
The family is the basic unit of society.

senses.def: a standard amount used for measuring
ex: The metre is a unit of length.

senses.def: to join together to form a group or to act as one
ex: The two parties united to win the election.
The tragedy united the whole town.

senses.def: joined together by a shared aim or feeling
ex: The team stayed united during hard times.
We must present a united front.

senses.def: affecting or including everyone or everything in the world or a group
ex: Music is a universal language.
The idea has universal appeal.

senses.def: all of space and everything in it, including stars and planets
ex: Scientists study how the universe began.
There may be life elsewhere in the universe.

senses.def: a place where students study for a degree after leaving school
ex: She studies law at university.
He is applying to several universities.

mistake.wrong: She is studying in the university of Cairo.
mistake.right: She is studying at the University of Cairo.
mistake.note: Use 'at' with university, and capital letters with the full name; no article is used in 'at university'.

senses.def: not known, or not familiar to people
ex: The cause of the fire is unknown.
She is an unknown singer from a small town.

senses.def: except if; used to say that something will happen only if something else does not happen
ex: I won't go unless you come with me.
Don't call unless it is urgent.

mistake.wrong: Unless you don't hurry, you will miss the bus.
mistake.right: Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.
mistake.note: Unless already means 'if not', so the verb after it is positive.

senses.def: not likely to happen or be true
ex: It's unlikely that it will snow tomorrow.
He is unlikely to win.

senses.def: without any limit in number or amount
ex: The hotel offers unlimited internet access.
We have unlimited time to finish.

senses.def: to remove goods from a vehicle or container
ex: Workers unloaded the boxes from the truck.
The ship is unloading at the port.

senses.def: to open a lock using a key or code
ex: He unlocked the front door.
Enter your code to unlock the phone.

senses.def: to make something possible that was not possible before
ex: Education can unlock a child's potential.

senses.def: having bad luck, or causing bad luck
ex: We were unlucky to lose by one goal.
Some people think thirteen is an unlucky number.

senses.def: operated without a person on board
ex: An unmanned spacecraft landed on the moon.
They use unmanned aircraft to take photos.

senses.def: different from what is normal or expected, often in a strange way
ex: There was an unnatural silence in the room.
Her smile looked unnatural.

senses.def: making you feel nervous or slightly afraid
ex: It was unnerving to hear footsteps behind me.
The quiet in the old house was unnerving.

senses.def: to disconnect a piece of electrical equipment by pulling its plug out of the socket
ex: Unplug the iron when you finish.
Please unplug the kettle before cleaning it.

senses.def: changing often so that you cannot know what will happen next
ex: The weather here is unpredictable.
He is an unpredictable person.

senses.def: to separate threads that are twisted together, or to become undone
ex: The cat unravelled the ball of wool.
The scarf began to unravel.

senses.def: to understand or solve something that is complicated or mysterious
ex: Detectives are trying to unravel the mystery.

senses.def: not fair or sensible
ex: It is unreasonable to expect results so quickly.
The price seems unreasonable.

senses.def: not able to be trusted or depended on
ex: The old bus service is unreliable.
He is an unreliable worker who is often late.

senses.def: dangerous or likely to cause harm
ex: The building is unsafe after the fire.
She felt unsafe walking home alone.

senses.def: making you feel worried or uncomfortable
ex: The news was deeply unsettling.
There was something unsettling about his smile.

senses.def: so strong or powerful that it cannot be stopped
ex: The team seemed unstoppable this season.
Change is unstoppable.

senses.def: not certain about something, or lacking confidence
ex: I'm unsure whether to accept the job.
She felt unsure of herself.

senses.def: to undo a knot or something that is tied
ex: She untied the ribbon and opened the box.
Can you untie my shoelaces?

senses.def: up to the time that something happens or ends
ex: The shop is open until nine o'clock.
I waited until midnight.

senses.def: up to the time when something happens
ex: Wait here until I come back.
We played until it got dark.

mistake.wrong: I will wait until he will come.
mistake.right: I will wait until he comes.
mistake.note: After until, use a present tense, not will, for future meaning.

senses.def: to; used mainly in old or religious language
ex: Do unto others as you would have them do unto you.

senses.def: different from what is normal or expected
ex: It's unusual for him to be late.
She has an unusual name.

senses.def: towards or in a higher place
ex: We walked up the hill.
The cat ran up the tree.

senses.def: towards a higher position or level
ex: Please stand up.
Prices have gone up again.

senses.def: out of bed
ex: What time do you get up?

senses.def: the way that parents care for and teach their children
ex: She had a strict upbringing.
His upbringing taught him to respect others.

senses.def: to make something more modern or add the latest information
ex: Please update your address on the form.
I need to update my phone's software.

senses.def: a new piece of information or a new version of something
ex: Here is a quick update on the project.
The app needs a software update.

senses.def: a newer or better version of something, or a move to a higher level of service
ex: The hotel gave us a free room upgrade.
The upgrade will improve the system's speed.

senses.def: to make something better or replace it with a newer one
ex: We upgraded our computers last year.
She upgraded to business class.

senses.def: on; more formal than 'on'
ex: Once upon a time there was a king.
Upon arrival, please sign in at the desk.

senses.def: higher in position, level or rank
ex: She has a scar on her upper lip.
They live on the upper floor.

senses.def: standing or sitting straight up
ex: Please keep your seat in an upright position.

senses.def: honest and fair in your behaviour
ex: He was an upright citizen respected by all.

senses.def: in a straight and vertical position
ex: She sat upright in bed.

senses.def: unhappy, worried or angry because of something unpleasant
ex: She was upset when she heard the news.
Don't be upset – it was only a mistake.

senses.def: slightly ill in the stomach
ex: He has an upset stomach.

senses.def: to make someone feel unhappy, worried or angry
ex: I'm sorry if I upset you.
The film upset the children.

senses.def: to or on a higher floor of a building
ex: She went upstairs to bed.
The children are playing upstairs.

senses.def: on a higher floor of a building
ex: The upstairs bathroom is being repaired.

senses.def: the upper floors of a building
ex: The upstairs is made up of three bedrooms.

senses.def: relating to towns and cities
ex: More people now live in urban areas.
Urban traffic is a serious problem.

senses.def: a strong feeling that you want to do something
ex: I felt an urge to laugh.
He resisted the urge to shout.

senses.def: to strongly advise or try to persuade someone to do something
ex: Doctors urge people to exercise regularly.
She urged him to see a lawyer.

senses.def: needing to be dealt with immediately
ex: I have an urgent message for you.
The patient needs urgent medical care.

senses.def: in a way that needs immediate action
ex: The village urgently needs clean water.
She called urgently for a doctor.

senses.def: used as the object of a verb or after a preposition to mean the speaker and others
ex: Please help us.
They invited us to dinner.

senses.def: to do something with a tool, machine or method to get a result
ex: Can I use your phone?
We use a computer every day.

senses.def: the act of using something, or a purpose for something
ex: The use of mobile phones is not allowed here.
This old box has many uses.

mistake.wrong: I use to go to school by bus.
mistake.right: I used to go to school by bus.
mistake.note: For past habits write 'used to' with a d; 'use to' only appears after did/didn't.

senses.def: be used to something: familiar with it because you have often done or seen it
ex: I'm used to getting up early.
She isn't used to the cold weather.

senses.def: not new; owned by someone before
ex: He bought a used car.

mistake.wrong: I am used to get up early.
mistake.right: I am used to getting up early.
mistake.note: After 'be used to' use the -ing form, because to is a preposition here.

senses.def: helpful for doing or achieving something
ex: This is a useful website for learning English.
Thanks, that was very useful.

senses.def: having no value or not working well
ex: This old phone is useless.
It's useless to argue with him.

senses.def: a person who uses a product, service or machine
ex: The website has a million users.
Most users prefer the new design.

senses.def: to show someone politely where to go
ex: A waiter ushered us to our table.

senses.def: a person who shows people to their seats in a theatre or at a wedding
ex: The usher showed us to our seats.

senses.def: happening, done or used most often; normal
ex: She woke up at the usual time.
It's quieter than usual today.

senses.def: a public service such as electricity, gas or water
ex: The rent includes utilities such as water and gas.
Utility bills rose this winter.

senses.def: the quality of being useful
ex: The tool has little practical utility.

senses.def: to say something or make a sound with your voice
ex: He did not utter a word.
She uttered a cry of surprise.

senses.def: complete or total
ex: The film was an utter waste of time.
She looked at him in utter disbelief.

senses.def: completely or extremely
ex: The idea is utterly ridiculous.
He was utterly exhausted.
